parameters.content:
## KYC/AML Monitoring Workflow

Starter template from agentmelt.com — configure before running:

1. Fill in "Config (edit me)" (name, approver, quiet hours; test_mode stays on for the first week).
2. Add credentials to every service node (Anthropic, mail, CRM, database…).
3. Replace placeholder URLs, queries and field mappings with yours.
4. Set the trigger: New customers screened at onboarding; the full book re-screened daily against list updates; transaction events evaluated in near real time.
5. Keep the gates: 'Needs a person?' after every AI step, 'Approved?' after the approval — wire their dead ends to a sheet or a channel.
6. Keep the guardrails:
   - No case is closed without an analyst's recorded decision; the agent drafts, never decides.
   - Sanctions matches always reach a senior analyst regardless of the draft assessment.
   - Every decision is logged in a tamper-evident store with actor, rationale and timestamp.
   - Rules and thresholds are versioned; changes require compliance-officer approval and are logged.

Full blueprint and pricing: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/kyc-aml-monitoring/
Want it built and run for you? $297/month · custom $8,000–15,000 one-time

assignments.name: config.approver
assignments.value: #approvals — a Slack channel, or an email address

nodes.name: Config (edit me)
nodes.notes:
Fill these in once; every later node reads them as $('Config (edit me)').item.json.config.*

test_mode = true: log what the workflow would write, without writing it, for the first week.
approval_mode = true: the approval node waits for a person; switch off per message type once it has earned it.

Also point the nodes at your own sources:
- Onboarding system / CRM (customer profiles)
- Screening providers (ComplyAdvantage, Dow Jones, Refinitiv, OpenSanctions)
- Core banking / payments (transactions)
- Compliance rule set and risk policy

options.systemMessage:
You are the "Pre-assess matches" step of the KYC/AML Monitoring Workflow workflow run by Agentmelt.
Task: For each hit the agent compares the customer profile to the list entry — dates, locations, identifiers, context — and drafts an assessment: likely true match, likely false positive, or needs more information, with the reasoning.

Rules:
- No case is closed without an analyst's recorded decision; the agent drafts, never decides.
- Sanctions matches always reach a senior analyst regardless of the draft assessment.
- Every decision is logged in a tamper-evident store with actor, rationale and timestamp.
- Rules and thresholds are versioned; changes require compliance-officer approval and are logged.
- Answer only from the data provided in the input. If something is missing, say so in the output instead of guessing.
- If this step produces a message or a document, put the full text in `draft` (and a `subject` if it is an email); put a one-line summary in `summary`.
- Set `needs_human` true whenever you are unsure, the input is unusual, or a rule above applies; a person will look at it.
- Return valid JSON matching the output schema; no prose outside the JSON.

nodes.name: AI Agent: Pre-assess matches
nodes.notes:
Pre-assess matches

For each hit the agent compares the customer profile to the list entry — dates, locations, identifiers, context — and drafts an assessment: likely true match, likely false positive, or needs more information, with the reasoning.

nodes.name: Needs a person?
nodes.notes: True = the AI step was not sure or flagged the item → dead letter, a person looks. False = continue. Wire the dead letter to a Slack message or a sheet so nothing fails silently.

nodes.name: Needs a person: Pre-assess matches
nodes.notes: Dead letter. Replace this no-op with a Slack message or a sheet row that carries the raw item and the reason — silent failures are the ones that cost.

nodes.name: Code: Evaluate transactions
nodes.notes:
Evaluate transactions

Rule set (structuring patterns, velocity, high-risk corridors, unusual counterparties) applied to transaction events; rules versioned and owned by compliance.

nodes.name: Set: Build the case
nodes.notes:
Build the case

Alert, customer profile, screening evidence, transaction history and the agent's draft assembled into a case record.

nodes.name: Slack approval: Route to the analyst
nodes.notes:
Route to the analyst

Cases queued by risk score; low-risk likely-false-positives can be batch-cleared with a review sample; anything involving sanctions goes to a senior analyst.

Send-and-wait: the run pauses here until someone presses Approve or Reject. Set config.approver in "Config (edit me)".

nodes.name: Approved?
nodes.notes: True = approved → continue to the write-back. False = rejected → stop here; the item stays where it was.

nodes.name: Rejected: Route to the analyst
nodes.notes: Rejected by the approver. Nothing is written. Optionally log the rejection to your sheet so the weekly count of corrections is visible.

nodes.name: Postgres: Record the decision
nodes.notes:
Record the decision

Analyst decision, rationale, reviewer and timestamp recorded on the case in a tamper-evident log; SAR/STR drafts generated for confirmed suspicious cases.

nodes.name: Schedule Trigger: Continuous re-screening
nodes.notes:
Continuous re-screening

Daily re-screen against list updates; changes in a customer's risk (new PEP status, adverse media) reopen a case automatically.

nodes.name: Google Docs: Regulatory reporting
nodes.notes:
Regulatory reporting

Monthly MI: alerts by type, false-positive rate, clearance times, open cases by age, and the rule-tuning log.
